question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and which deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules should decide allow, require-confirm, deny, and timeout behavior?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing gate, but the permanent policy defines a new authorization boundary and config contract that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design core gate
options.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and regression coverage around existing plugin approvals.

options.title: Keep plugin-only
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged and require operators to implement contextual approvals through before_tool_call.requireApproval or trusted tool policies, accepting that no built-in same-response confirmation gate exists.

options.title: Defer into broader policy work
options.body: Wait for related action-level deny, response-gate, and HITL interrupt designs to settle into one authorization model before adding a new config surface.

recommendation.title: Design core gate
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-led core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and regression coverage around existing plugin approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans security defaults, config compatibility, and the agent-core execution loop, and prior live issue review already routed it to core product/security design.
